name: AI Certifications: Which to Get and How to Prepare
objectives: Given a credential description, explain whether it is a certificate of completion or a proctored certification and what it shows an employer, getting at least 4 of 5 right
Given several beginner AI credentials, compare them by provider, cost, time and level, naming which one fits a beginner and which is more technical

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Certificates vs certifications, and why they matter
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Tell a course certificate from a proctored certification and explain what each shows an employer.
This lesson builds toward: Given a credential description, you will explain whether it is a certificate of completion or a proctored certification and what it shows an employer, getting at least 4 of 5 right.
A certificate of completion shows you finished a course. A certification usually means you passed a supervised (proctored) exam that tests your skills. Employers often value certifications more, but a good certificate still shows effort and new skills.
AI credentials range from beginner ("what is AI and how do I use it at work") to technical ("build AI solutions in the cloud"). Beginner ones help in office, customer service, sales and admin jobs. Technical ones help in IT and cloud jobs and often need some coding or cloud knowledge first.
A credential is not a job guarantee. It works best with a résumé that shows how you used the skill, even in a small project. Pair it with real practice.
Words to know:
- Certificate: proof you finished a course or program.
- Certification: a credential earned by passing an exam that tests your skills.
- Proctored exam: a test watched by a person or camera to prevent cheating.
- Credential: any certificate, certification or license that proves a skill.
Try it now: Write one job you want. Next to it, write whether a beginner AI credential or a technical one fits better, and why.
You can now tell a certificate from a certification and choose the right level for a job goal.

check.q: What does a certificate of completion show?
options: That you passed a supervised exam
That you are licensed by the state
check.why: A certificate of completion shows you finished a course.

check.q: An employer asks what your new AI credential proves. You passed a proctored exam. What do you say?
options: It shows I passed a supervised exam that tested my skills
It means I am guaranteed the job
It means I watched some videos
check.why: A certification usually means passing a proctored exam that tests skills.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: A tour of well-known beginner AI credentials
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Compare several beginner AI credentials by provider, cost, time and level.
This lesson builds toward: Given several beginner AI credentials, you will compare them by provider, cost, time and level, naming which one fits a beginner and which is more technical.
These were checked on the official pages in October 2026; always re-check before you pay. Google AI Essentials is a self-paced course by Google on Coursera, under 5 hours, with a certificate; in the U.S. and Canada it is $49 a month after a 7-day free trial. It suits people who want to use AI tools at work.
The AWS Certified AI Practitioner is a foundational Amazon Web Services certification: a 90-minute exam with 65 questions and a $100 fee. Google Cloud's Generative AI Leader certification has no prerequisites: 90 minutes, 50-60 questions, $99, valid for 3 years, taken online or at a test center.
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals now uses exam AI-901, updated in April 2026. Its price depends on your country, the passing score is 700, and it now expects some Python and Azure knowledge, so it is more technical than before. Microsoft offers a free practice assessment once you sign in.
Words to know:
- Foundational: the entry level of a certification track.
- Prerequisite: something you must have or know before you start.
Official sources:
- Grow with Google: Google AI Essentials
- AWS Certified AI Practitioner
- Google Cloud: Generative AI Leader
- Microsoft Learn: Exam AI-901
Try it now: Open the official page for two of these credentials. For each, write the exact name, provider, cost, length and who it is for. Note anything that changed since this course was written.
You can now compare beginner AI credentials using their official pages.

check.q: Which credential in the lesson is a self-paced course with a certificate, rather than a proctored exam?
check.why: Google AI Essentials is a self-paced course on Coursera that ends with a certificate.

check.q: You are brand new to AI and want to use AI tools in an office job. Which is the least likely fit right now?
options: Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (AI-901), which now expects some Python and Azure
check.why: AI-901 now expects some Python and Azure knowledge, so it is more technical.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Matching a credential to a job and a budget
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Pick one credential using real job posts, your budget and your time.
This lesson builds toward: Given five real job posts, your budget and your time, you will choose one credential and find out who might help pay for it, with a reason based on the job posts.
Start from jobs, not from credentials. Search for jobs you want and count which credentials and skills appear in the posts. If several mention a cloud platform, that platform's credential may be worth it.
Then compare total cost (fee, retake fee, any training), time to prepare, and your current level. If you are brand new, a short beginner course first may save you a failed exam fee.
Look for help paying. Workforce programs, American Job Centers, reentry programs, veterans benefits, libraries and some employers may pay for training or exams; some providers offer discounts or financial aid. Ask before you pay, and never pay someone who "guarantees" a pass or sells exam answers: that is a scam and can get your credential cancelled.
Step by step:
- Find five job posts you want.
- Count which credentials and skills they mention.
- Compare total cost, time and level for your top two.
- Ask your workforce or reentry program about paying for it.
- Pick one.
Words to know:
- Retake fee: what you pay to take an exam again if you do not pass.
- Financial aid: help paying for education or training.
Try it now: Find five job posts you want and list the AI or tech credentials they mention. Pick one credential and write its total cost and who might help pay for it.
You can now choose a credential that fits real jobs, your budget and your time.

check.q: What is included in the total cost of a credential?
options: The exam fee, any retake fee and any training
check.why: Total cost includes the fee, retakes and training.

check.q: Three of your five job posts mention the same cloud platform. What do you consider?
options: That platform's credential, and ask a workforce program about help paying
A random credential from an ad
Buying exam answers to save time
check.why: Start from job posts; a platform mentioned often may make its credential worth it.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Reading the official exam page
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Pull the key facts from an official exam page into a one-page fact sheet.
This lesson builds toward: Using the credential's official exam page, you will write a one-page fact sheet of the exam's name, cost, format, skills measured, ID and retake rules and how long it stays valid, with every fact from the official page and the date you checked.
The official exam page is the only source you should trust for exam facts. Look for: the exact name and exam code, price, length and number of questions, passing score, languages, how you can take it (online or test center), skills measured and their weight, and how long the credential is valid.
The skills-measured list, sometimes called the exam guide or study guide, is your map. If a topic is 40% of the exam, it deserves about 40% of your study time.
Check the rules too: ID required (often a current government-issued photo ID with a name that matches your registration), online testing room rules, rescheduling deadlines and retake policies. If your ID situation is complicated, solve it early.
Step by step:
- Open the provider's official exam page.
- Write the name, code, price, length, questions and passing score.
- Copy the skills measured with their percentages.
- Note ID, testing and retake rules.
- Save the page link and the date you checked.
Words to know:
- Exam code: the short code for an exam, like AI-901.
- Skills measured: the list of topics an exam tests, often with percentages.
- Passing score: the score you need to pass.
Try it now: Make a one-page fact sheet for your chosen credential from its official page, including skills measured with percentages, ID rules and the date you checked.
You can now read an official exam page and turn it into a fact sheet.

check.q: What is the skills-measured list on an exam page?
options: Your map of what the exam tests and how much each topic counts
A list of past test takers
check.why: The skills-measured list shows each topic and its weight on the exam.

check.q: Your ID has a different last name from the one you will register with. What do you do?
options: Solve it early, because the ID name must match the registration
check.why: The ID name often must match the registration, so fix it early.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Building a study plan with free training and AI
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Make a four-week study plan using free official training, AI tutoring and practice tests.
This lesson builds toward: Given the skills measured and free official training, you will create a four-week study plan that uses AI as a tutor and includes a practice test, with study time matched to each topic's exam weight.
Most providers offer free training. Microsoft Learn has free learning paths and a free practice assessment for many exams; AWS Skill Builder and Google offer free learning too. Start there before paying for anything.
Use AI as a tutor, not a cheat. Ask: "Explain [topic from the skills list] in simple words with a real-world example. Then quiz me with five multiple-choice questions and explain my mistakes." Check anything that seems off against the official training, since AI can be wrong or out of date.
Plan four weeks: weeks 1-3 cover topics in order of their exam weight, a little each day; week 4 is practice tests and reviewing weak areas. Aim to score well on the official practice test before booking the real exam.
Step by step:
- List the skills measured and their weights.
- Find the free official training for each.
- Plan 30-60 minutes a day for weeks 1-3, heaviest topics first.
- Use AI to explain and quiz you; check against official training.
- Week 4: practice tests and weak spots.
Words to know:
- Learning path: a set of lessons in order on one topic.
- Practice test: a sample exam that shows what the real one is like.
Try it now: Write a four-week study plan for your credential. Then ask an AI assistant to explain one topic from the skills list and quiz you with five questions.
You can now build a study plan with free training, AI tutoring and practice tests.

check.q: In the four-week plan, what is week 4 for?
options: Practice tests and reviewing weak areas
check.why: Week 4 is for practice tests and weak spots.

check.q: AI explains a topic one way, but the official training says something different. What do you do?
options: Ask the AI again until it agrees
check.why: AI can be wrong or out of date; the official training is the trusted source.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Getting ready for exam day and using your credential
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Prepare for exam day and add your new credential to your résumé and profiles.
This lesson builds toward: Before and after the exam, you will prepare for exam day and add the credential to your résumé, with the exact name, provider and date.
Before exam day, test your setup if you are taking it online: most providers have a system check. Clear your desk and room as the rules say. For a test center, plan your route and arrive early with the right ID.
During the exam: read each question twice, answer the easy ones first, flag hard ones and come back, and do not leave any blank unless the rules say wrong answers cost points.
After you pass, add it to your résumé under "Certifications" with the exact name, provider and date, and claim any digital badge the provider offers to share online. If you do not pass, read the score report, study the weak areas and use the retake policy. Many people pass on the second try.
Step by step:
- Run the online system check or plan your route.
- Prepare your ID and room as the rules require.
- On the exam, read twice, do easy ones first, flag hard ones.
- After passing, add it to your résumé with exact name, provider and date.
- If not, study weak areas from the score report and retake.
Words to know:
- System check: a test that your computer, camera and internet work for an online exam.
- Digital badge: an online image that proves you earned a credential.
- Score report: the results showing how you did on each part of the exam.
Try it now: Final task: complete your fact sheet and four-week study plan, take one official practice test or AI quiz, and book a study start date or exam date. Write how the credential will appear on your résumé.
You can now choose, prepare for and use an AI credential that fits your job goal.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Credential matches a job The credential is not linked to a real job post. One credential chosen and linked to a real job post the learner wants. Compared two options by total cost, time and level, and asked a program about help paying. Official facts Facts are missing or come from somewhere other than the official page. Exact name, provider, cost, length and format, skills measured, ID rules and how long it is valid, from the official page. Includes the page link, the date checked and the retake policy. Four-week study plan No plan, or no practice test. Four weeks using free official training, heaviest topics first, with at least one practice test. Includes AI tutoring prompts and a check against official training. Exam booked and ready No practice session or exam date. A practice session or exam date is booked and ID needs are known. System check done or route planned, and a note on how the credential will go on the résumé. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: What should you do before an online proctored exam?
options: Run the provider's system check and prepare your room
check.why: A system check and a room set up by the rules prevent problems on exam day.

check.q: You passed. How do you list it on your résumé?
options: Under Certifications, with the exact name, provider and date
Leave it off until someone asks
check.why: List the exact name, provider and date under Certifications.
